finding: DISCLOSURE — this round is NOT a blind multi-angle audit. The session that ran it was explicitly instructed not to spawn subagents, so the angles below were applied by the same agent that finished the implementation, from the committed diff. Independence is genuinely weaker than the phase-6 discipline intends: a blind reviewer cannot be primed by the author's reasoning, and this one was. Every finding is therefore backed by a RUN (a probe, a lint run, a measurement), not by an assertion, and AUD-1 is recorded with its failed reproduction rather than as a confirmed bug. Re-running phase 6 with fresh reviewers is the honest follow-up.

AUD-1 — no-row guard was `loading && !settings`, but 'no row' and 'a fetch is in flight' are not the same condition: schedulerAdminState initialises `loading:false`, the fetch is kicked off by a post-commit effect, and loadSettings early-returns WITHOUT setting `loading` when hasPermissionNow(SchedulerAdminRead) is false. Because `useForm`'s defaultValues ARE the server's own defaults, any render in that state shows five plausible, authoritative-looking numbers the page does not have, and one edit + Save PUTs the other four over the real row. REPRODUCTION FAILED for the stronger 'it flashes today' claim: with the weak guard restored, the gallery `delayed` mode (reads held 700ms, page chunk pre-warmed, 25ms sampling) still rendered the Spin at 500ms and no form — React flushes the mount effect before paint. Downgraded from high to medium and fixed as hardening + precedent-fidelity (RetrievalLimitsSection gates on `!settings`), with TEST-9 pinning the window's behaviour either way.

AUD-2 — TEST-5a asserted `<= 2 lines` over EVERY multi-word label on the whole document, but its TESTS.md claim is about the Limits form. Any unrelated multi-word label in the shared settings chrome would fail this spec and blame this page; conversely the assertion never checks that the five Limits labels are actually present (a page that rendered zero of them would satisfy `labels.length >= 5` only by accident of the chrome). Rewritten to look up the five known label texts by name and assert presence + line count on each.

AUD-3 — `collectStarvedLabelsIn(root)` was exported and never called by anything (grep over tests/ + src/): dead code on arrival, and its text-set matching would have cross-matched two identical label texts in different containers. CODING_GUIDELINES §15 (dead code = unfinished work). Removed, along with the now-unused Locator import.

AUD-4 — moving the unit out of the label text and into the control `suffix` (DEC-3) removes it from the accessible name: measured, each input's accessible name is now exactly 'Minimum interval' / 'Self-paced loop horizon' / 'Notification retention', and the suffix element is not in the aria-labelledby or aria-describedby chain, so a screen-reader user hears a bare number with no unit. The pre-fix labels said '(seconds)' / '(days)'. This is a house-wide trait of the `suffix` convention (SessionSettingsPage's `suffix="hours"`/`"days"` has it too), so the fix keeps the convention and restores the unit in the field `description` — which IS in aria-describedby (measured: describedby present on all five).

AUD-5 — INV-1/INV-2 (DESIGN_SYSTEM 'Form & settings layout': compose Field/FormField, never a hand-rolled label+control row) verified against the DESIGN, not the plan: the shipped page routes all five controls through <Form layout="horizontal"> + <FormField>, and the rendered proof is 0 starved labels at 1280/768/390 where the pre-fix page had 5 at 1280 and 768. INV-3 (actions in the Card footer via SettingsFormActions) and INV-4 (semantic tokens, 4px rhythm, logical direction) hold — `npm run check` EXIT=0 chains lint:colors + lint:logical-direction + check:design-spec. INV-6 (mirror the sibling, don't invent) holds: the card is a transcription of RetrievalLimitsSection down to the `!mb-3 text-sm` intro Paragraph. No divergence found; recorded so the required angle is on the record with its evidence.

AUD-6 — the rebuild drops the persistent inline error Alert that the pre-fix page rendered above the card, leaving a failed SAVE surfaced only by a transient toast. Checked against both named siblings before calling it: SessionSettingsPage (the PAGE twin this shell is copied from) also renders no inline error in its loaded state — only RetrievalLimitsSection (a SECTION, not a page) keeps one. Following the page twin is the documented intent (DEC-1) and diverging from it to satisfy the section twin would be the drift this lifecycle exists to prevent. NOT a defect; recorded as reviewed.

AUD-7 — double-submit: `saveDisabled` is `!canManage || !isDirty`, and the form stays dirty for the whole in-flight PUT, so the Save is NOT disabled by that expression while saving. Checked the kit Button: `loading` sets `pointer-events-none opacity-70` AND replaces onClick with `e.preventDefault()` (kit/button.tsx:141-146), so a second activation is swallowed. `saving` is threaded through SettingsFormActions -> Button `loading`. No second PUT is reachable. NOT a defect.

AUD-8 — the `settings && !form.formState.isDirty` re-seed guard means a cross-device save silently does NOT reach a page with unsaved local edits (last-writer-wins on the next local save). Verified this is the copied behaviour of both siblings (SessionSettingsPage:38-45, RetrievalLimitsSection:56-64) and is the intended tradeoff (clobbering an admin's in-progress typing is worse). `form.reset(v)` after a successful save re-opens the page to re-seeding, so the guard cannot latch permanently once a row has been saved. NOT a defect.

AUD-9 — the branch introduces NO permission (verified: the diff touches no permissions.rs and no migration), so A9/A10 do not apply. But DEC-10 CHANGES the read-only path's behaviour (the footer now renders disabled instead of being omitted) and that path has no automated coverage before or after this branch: the route requires scheduler_admin::read, so exercising read-without-manage needs a purpose-built group + user, and the gallery's data-page states carry no permission axis. Recorded as GAP-1 in INFRA_INTEGRATION.md and surfaced to the owner rather than claimed as covered. Not closed here — closing it properly is a harness change (a permission axis on page-surface gallery states, or a read-only user fixture), which is larger than this fix.

AUD-10 — `updateSettings(v)` PUTs all five keys on every save, including four the admin did not touch. Checked: this is unchanged from the pre-fix page (which also sent the whole `f` object), the store action's type is `UpdateSchedulerAdminSettings` (tsc clean), and with the AUD-1 guard in place the five values always originate from a real server row. No contract change, no regression. NOT a defect.

AUD-11 — branch ORDER: the error branch must precede the no-row branch. With the AUD-1 fix, `!settings` is now true whenever there is no row INCLUDING after a failed load, so an error-second ordering would have replaced the retryable ErrorState with an endless spinner and made the failure unrecoverable without a page reload. Fixed by ordering `error && !settings` first, and pinned in the code comment. The gallery `error` state renders the ErrorState (RUNTIME_FINDINGS records the deliberate 'Internal server error' console line for settings-scheduler:error, so that cell really is exercised).

AUD-12 — TEST-9 introduces a `page.route()` into a spec whose whole point (DEC-12, TESTING_GUIDE, CODING_GUIDELINES §14) is that it drives the REAL backend with no mocking. Resolved by making it a THROTTLE, not a mock: the handler sleeps and then calls `route.continue()`, so the real server serves the real body and no response is ever fabricated. R2-5 also satisfied — `/api/scheduler/admin-settings` is a live route (it is what the store's ApiClient.SchedulerAdminSettings calls), not a renamed path that would make the interception a silent no-op.

AUD-13 — FB-17: is each deliverable actually INVOKED on a real path, or merely present and unit-tested? Checked all three. (1) The visual spec is in `gallery.config.json -> visualSpecs`, which is what gate:ui reads, and it RAN: 8/8 under playwright.visual.config.ts. (2) The static lint is in `npm run check` via `lint:settings-field` and RAN in both directions on the real tree (5 violations pre-fix / 0 post-fix). (3) The rig detector is the one that could have been dead — so it was executed as SOURCE: sliced verbatim out of live-ui-audit.mjs and evaluated in-page, producing 5 findings pre-fix with the identical metrics and 0 post-fix. None of the three is present-but-unreached.

AUD-14 — is the gating sweep vacuously green? Checked three ways. (a) The detector-acceptance leg injects the EXACT pre-fix markup next to a correct row in the same 840px container and asserts flagged/not-flagged — so a probe that silently returned [] would fail. (b) The sweep asserts `surfaces.length > 20` so an empty enumeration cannot pass. (c) Empirically re-run on the pre-fix tree: 5 starved on `settings-scheduler`, i.e. the sweep genuinely goes red on the defect it was written for. RESIDUAL WEAKNESS, recorded not hidden: each surface settles on a fixed `waitForTimeout(1200)`, so a slower surface can be measured before it paints its form — that direction fails OPEN (a missed detection), never closed (a false red).

AUD-15 — the mobile (390px) leg of the sweep would NOT have caught this defect: measured on the pre-fix tree, 390px reports 0 starved labels, because clause 3 ('the row had room', rowW >= 2x naturalW) correctly refuses to blame a ~340px row for an unavoidable wrap. Desktop and tablet are the legs that fire. Keeping the mobile leg as a regression guard is right; weakening clause 3 to make it fire would reintroduce exactly the flag-every-page failure mode the check exists to avoid. Recorded so nobody reads the mobile leg as the proof.

AUD-16 — the four starvation clauses now exist in THREE places: this helper, the agent-kit rig detector, and (as fixture numbers) the predicate tests. A shared import is not available across repo boundaries, so the duplication is structural rather than lazy. Mitigations in place: the thresholds live in one named `STARVATION` constant per copy, both copies carry the same calibration doc-comment, and their equivalence is PROVEN by execution rather than asserted (identical metrics on the same 5 labels, identical silence on 4 sibling surfaces). Recorded as a known maintenance cost, not a defect to fix by inventing a shared package for 60 lines.

AUD-17 — plan-coverage reconciliation, every ITEM against shipped code. ITEM-1 SchedulerAdminPage.tsx:175-251; ITEM-2 the five `className="w-40"` + `suffix`; ITEM-3 :144-157 footer/SettingsFormActions; ITEM-4 :98-133 + :159-173; ITEM-5 screenshots at 390/768/1280 x light/dark; ITEM-6 `npm run check` EXIT=0; ITEM-7 the AST census (79 files) + the rendered census (46 surfaces x 3 viewports); ITEM-8 sdk c9bf67f; ITEM-9 gallery.config.json:17 + the spec; ITEM-10 agent-kit fix/label-starvation-detector; ITEM-11 the 14-scheduler layout spec. No ITEM is unimplemented and none is [DESCOPED]. The one scope DRIFT is the reverse: ITEM-10's artifact deliberately does NOT ride the superproject pointer (DEC-7/DEC-8), so 'shipped on this branch' is false for it and the summary must say so.

AUD-18 — rule 2's STRETCHING set is a closed literal (`Input`,`InputNumber`,`InputPassword`,`Textarea`); a future kit control whose root carries w-full would be silently exempt until someone edits this file. Weighed against the alternative (infer w-full from the kit source at lint time) and kept closed on purpose: the set is derived from shadcn/input.tsx + shadcn/textarea.tsx and is stated as such in the rule's doc-comment, and a broader or inferred set is exactly what would make lint:settings-field — which sits inside `npm run check` for every branch — fire on the two correct pages (ThemeSettings, McpToolApprovalsTab). Documented, deliberate, and cheap to extend.

AUD-19 — TEST-5d mutates real deployment-wide scheduler limits (37 / 11) against a live backend. Checked the blast radius: per CLAUDE.md and playwright.config.ts every e2e test CREATEs its own `ziee_test_<id>` database and spawns its own backend, so the mutation cannot escape the test. The spec restores 20/30 anyway, which is harmless belt-and-braces. No credential, token or secret is read, logged, or asserted on anywhere in the diff. NOT a defect.

AUD-20 — copy review of the five labels + descriptions. 'Auto-pause after' + suffix 'failures' reads as one sentence in the row ('Auto-pause after [5] failures') and drops the pre-fix label's bare 'N', which was a placeholder leaking into user-facing copy. Every description states what the limit bounds AND what happens at the bound, which is the JTBD the plan set. Strings are English literals, consistent with the rest of the app (no i18n framework is in play on this stack), and the e2e selects by data-testid, not text — so the copy stays translatable without breaking tests. NOT a defect.
